sites.name: Almaden Mine
overview: Almaden Mine is a documented underground mine on the southwest side of Fall River. USGS studies describe two principal drift adits and a shaft, including workings on the Colorado No. 1 or Blazing Star vein, providing a defensible Basic Scan identity without asserting present-day access or condition.

timeline.text: Federal and Colorado School of Mines records document the Almaden property across multiple studies, including early mine reports and later USGS investigations of its polymetallic and uranium-bearing veins.

sites.name: AP Tunnel
overview: AP Tunnel is a documented underground gold-silver past producer on Kelso Mountain. A historic image identifies the mine's shafthouse and tailings, giving the site a stable Basic Scan identity while later chronology and present condition remain intentionally unasserted.

timeline.text: A contemporary Colorado Miner report described the A. P. tunnel as a developing ore-producing property.

sites.name: Apex Shaft
overview: Apex Shaft is a distinct underground gold past-producer locality in Clear Creek County. Federal mine records and mapped shaft data provide a stable Basic Scan anchor while site-specific operator and production chronology remain incomplete.

timeline.text: USGS and MRDS records preserve Apex Shaft as a named underground gold mine and past producer.

sites.name: Brighton Mine
overview: Brighton Mine is a documented Freeland-Lamartine underground mine with a long early-20th-century operating span and recorded gold, silver, lead, copper, and zinc production. The federal mine record provides a stable Basic Scan anchor without requiring any claim about present-day remnants.

timeline.text: Federal records document sustained work and production at Brighton during the early and mid-20th century.

sites.name: Brownsville Processing Plant
overview: Brownsville is a federally recorded gold processing plant and past-producer locality in Clear Creek County. The plant identity and mapped position are sufficient for Basic Scan while construction date, operator, process, throughput, feed mines, and surviving features remain intentionally unresolved.

timeline.text: Federal mineral records preserve Brownsville as a named gold-processing plant and past producer.

sites.name: Bullion King Mine
overview: Bullion King, also recorded as Mayflower, is a documented underground gold-polymetallic past producer in Clear Creek County. Federal records preserve the alias relationship, mapped entrance, 1902–1906 production period, and commodity mix for a defensible Basic Scan record.

timeline.text: Federal records document production at the Bullion King/Mayflower property during this period.

sites.name: Nonpareil Mine
overview: Nonpareil Mine is a documented historic underground gold mine in Clear Creek County's Dumont area. Federal mineral records preserve the mine as a past producer and provide a stable mapped location for identification.

timeline.text: Federal mineral records identify Nonpareil as a past-producing underground gold mine in the Dumont district.

moreHistory: USGS mineral-record data place the Nonpareil Mine near 39.74972, -105.52250 at about 7,999 feet elevation and record a polymetallic-vein setting with pyrite and sphalerite. The retained sources do not establish a dependable operator chronology, production total, or surviving surface features, so those details are left unstated.

sourceReferences.title: Mindat bibliography entry for USGS Open-File Report 66-87

sites.name: Alabama Shaft
overview: Alabama Shaft is a documented historic gold-silver shaft and mine locality in Clear Creek County's Lamartine Mining District.

USGS-derived topographic mapping preserves the named shaft near 39.73721, -105.58667, providing a defensible mine-level identification anchor without asserting that any historic surface structure survives today.
moreHistory: Federal mine inventories preserve Alabama Shaft as a named past-producing Clear Creek County locality. The mapped point identifies the historic shaft property; Remnant does not claim that the shaft collar, a headframe, hoist house, ore bins, or other surface remains have been field-verified or are accessible.
A focused exact-site media search did not produce a defensible reusable historical photograph, so unrelated district imagery was rejected rather than attached to the wrong site.

sites.name: Accord Mine
overview: Accord Mine is a documented historic mine in Clear Creek County near Empire. USGS-derived topographic mapping preserves the named mine at approximately 39.746654, -105.668614, providing a defensible identification point without implying present-day access or surviving open workings.
moreHistory: The mapped Accord Mine is identified as an inactive gold-and-silver mine on the Georgetown, Colorado topographic quadrangle. The available retained evidence supports the mine's identity and location, but does not establish a reliable operator chronology, production total, or present condition, so those details are left unstated.
